result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.text:
MEMO - March 2026 Close: Unrecorded Liabilities / AP Cutoff Review (Search for Unrecorded Liabilities)

To: Controller
From: David Murguia, Senior Accountant
Date: 2026-04-03
Subject: Review of April 2026 invoices and payments; March accruals posted

PURPOSE
Auditors will perform a search for unrecorded liabilities. I reviewed all post-close (April 2026) vendor invoices and disbursement activity available in the document store and accrued into March everything for which the goods or services were received on or before 2026-03-31, per Accounting Policy Manual s.5 ("Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received").

POPULATION REVIEWED
The complete subsequent-period population available is DOC-0206 through DOC-0210, all relating to Halvard Systems Inc. (US):
- DOC-0206 Lumen Office Leasing LOL-2026-04, dated 2026-04-01, USD 14,500.00
- DOC-0207 Pinecrest Janitorial PJ-0402, dated 2026-04-03, USD 780.00
- DOC-0208 Cirrus CDN CC-20260406, dated 2026-04-06, USD 3,200.00
- DOC-0209 Whitcombe & Ames LLP WA-3402, dated 2026-04-08, USD 12,400.00
- DOC-0210 US April AP payment register, 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-10 (all four invoices above were paid in this window)

I confirmed none of these four items was already recorded in the March ledger (no ledger activity for Pinecrest, Cirrus or Whitcombe in any period; GL 2100 Accrued Expenses had no March activity prior to my entries), so there is no double-count risk.

CONCLUSIONS AND ENTRIES POSTED (all dated 2026-03-31, US, credit 2100 Accrued Expenses)

ACCRUED IN MARCH - service delivery date precedes 2026-03-31:
1. JE-00304 - USD 780.00 - Dr 6120 Facilities & Cleaning / Cr 2100.
   Pinecrest Janitorial, deep cleaning performed 2026-03-28. Invoice date (4/3) is after the service date; the service was received in March. Support: DOC-0207, DOC-0210.
2. JE-00305 - USD 3,200.00 - Dr 5000 Hosting & Infrastructure / Cr 2100.
   Cirrus CDN, invoice states service period March 2026. Classic services-received-not-yet-invoiced accrual. Support: DOC-0208, DOC-0210.
3. JE-00306 - USD 12,400.00 - Dr 6500 Legal Fees / Cr 2100.
   Whitcombe & Ames LLP, invoice states legal services rendered March 2026. Support: DOC-0209, DOC-0210.
   *** This entry exceeds my USD 10,000 per-entry posting authority (Policy s.1). I posted it as a single entry (I did NOT split it, which s.1 prohibits) and immediately routed it to you via request_approval. It is currently PENDING APPROVAL and must be approved before the period is closed. ***

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED - does not belong in March:
4. DOC-0206, Lumen Office Leasing LOL-2026-04, USD 14,500.00 - NOT accrued.
   The invoice is explicitly for "Office rent, April 2026," i.e. the right-of-use benefit is received in April. Paying it on 2026-04-03 does not make it a March liability. I also confirmed March rent was already correctly expensed: GL 6100 Rent shows March activity of exactly USD 14,500 (invoice LUM-88858, paid 2026-03-05 per BT-US-0060), so March rent is complete and accruing April rent would double-count the annual charge. Also consistent with s.5: quotes/proposals and future-period costs are not liabilities. Note this is a period cost, not a prepaid under s.4, because coverage begins in the month immediately following and does not span more than one month.

NET EFFECT ON MARCH (US)
Total accrued: USD 16,380.00. GL 2100 Accrued Expenses March activity is a credit of 16,380.00; ending balance USD 54,580.00 credit. March pre-tax income decreases by USD 16,380.00 (6120 +780, 5000 +3,200, 6500 +12,400).

These three accruals should be reversed in April 2026 when the vendor invoices are entered into AP, to avoid duplicating the expense.

EXCEPTION LOGGED - EXC-001 (scope limitation, UK and DE)
All available subsequent-period evidence is US-only. There are no April 2026 vendor invoices, no April AP payment register, and no vendor statements for Halvard Systems Ltd (UK) or Halvard Systems GmbH (DE). I could not perform a subsequent-disbursements search for those two entities and therefore cannot conclude that their March liabilities are complete. I did not post any estimated or plug accrual for UK/DE, per policy s.11. Please have AP provide the 2026-04-01 to 2026-04-10 payment registers and unposted-invoice logs for UK and DE so the test can be completed before fieldwork; the auditors will almost certainly request them.

CHECKLIST
US "AP cutoff review" marked complete. UK and DE "AP cutoff review" left open pending the information requested in EXC-001.

ITEMS REQUIRING YOUR ACTION
1. Approve JE-00306 (USD 12,400) - currently pending.
2. Resolve EXC-001 by obtaining UK/DE April AP data.
